role: Pure, Sendable overnight statistics computation for OvernightChartsView (RR→HR, rolling RMSSD, peak HRV, sleep duration, organized-zone fallback with archive backfill) plus the view extension that fetches Apple Watch HR from HealthKit for sleep segments the Polar recording does not cover.
types: OvernightStatsComputer: struct — Sendable value holding session/result/healthKitSleep that computes OvernightStats off the main actor
OvernightStatsComputer.StatsInputs: struct (private) — bundle of inputs for makeStats
OvernightStatsComputer.WindowFields: struct (private) — analysis window ms bounds and clock labels
OvernightStatsComputer.AnalysisWindow: struct (private) — analysis window ms and wall-clock dates
OvernightChartsView: extension — HealthKit HR gap-fill fetch helpers
SleepDurationFields: struct — minutes/formatted/deep/awakenings/efficiency/isFromHealthKit for the sleep card
toplevel: Only type declarations; OvernightStatsComputer conforms to Sendable so it can be captured by Task.detached in OvernightChartsView.loadOvernightStats.

flags.text: No unit test references OvernightStatsComputer, trimmedMeanHR, uncoveredWindows or any helper here; only OvernightSnapshotTests renders OvernightChartsView, whose stats load in an async .task.

units.does: Builds OvernightStats from session.rrSeries: resolves sleep bounds and segment ranges, computes full-recording and sleep-window HR values, nadir/peak HR, rolling RMSSD, then delegates assembly to makeStats. Returns OvernightStats.empty when there are no RR points or no HR values.

branches.cond: rrSeries is nil or has no points

branches.effect: nil → empty flags array (every beat treated as clean)

branches.cond: hrValues has a min and max and points has first/last
branches.effect: false (no HR values at all, e.g. RR-only data where no 10 s window had 5 clean beats): return OvernightStats.empty even though rolling RMSSD could be computed; true: makeStats

flags.text: When no HR value survives filtering the whole stats object becomes .empty, so the HRV chart and peak HRV are also blank although RMSSD needs no HR.

Sleep boundaries/segments are wall-clock offsets from session.startDate (HealthKit dates via MillisecondOffset) but are compared against RRPoint.t_ms, which is cumulative RR time that RRModels documents as drifting after BLE drops (no production resync of streamingCumulativeMs). On a streamed night with dropouts the sleep-window HR filter, the 30-70% peak band and chart x-positions are shifted relative to real time, so nadir/avg HR and peak HRV are taken over the wrong beats. Sessions built via DataSourceSelector re-base t_ms onto wallClockMs and are unaffected.

units.does: Assembles OvernightStats: peak HRV/avg RMSSD from findPeakHRV, nadir/min/max/trimmed-mean HR, window fields, sleep-duration fields, chart start/end, and organized recovery zones; healthKitHR starts empty.

branches.cond: peakHRV is nil (no rolling RMSSD sample)

branches.effect: peakHRVIndex/peakHRVTimeMs = 0 and the formatted peak time is the wall-clock time of t_ms 0 (session start), shown as a real time on the Peak HRV card subtitle

flags.text: With no rolling RMSSD sample the peak time label is formatted from t_ms 0, so the Peak HRV card shows '0 ms' with the session start time as if it were the peak time.

units.does: Resolves the analysis window via analysisWindowTimes and formats its start/end clock labels.
Forwards to deriveSleepDuration with the first point's t_ms and recording duration.

Returns HR values inside the sleep period: per-segment union (sorted by index) on split nights, else the single sleepStart..sleepEnd range; falls back to the caller's full-recording set when that yields nothing.

branches.cond: more than one sleep segment range
branches.effect: true: compute HR per segment and concatenate, sorted by index; false: single range sleepStartMs..sleepEndMs
true: log and use fallback (full recording HR); false: return filtered

units.does: Trimmed mean of HR: drops lowest/highest 5% when there are at least 10 values, else plain mean.

branches.effect: plain mean (NaN for 0 values, but caller guarantees non-empty); else 5th–95th percentile mean

units.does: Computes analysis window ms bounds, preferring result.windowStartMs/EndMs, else indexing points by result.windowStart/windowEnd, and converts both to wall-clock dates.

branches.cond: result carries both windowStartMs and windowEndMs
branches.effect: true: use them; false: derive from indices
true: points[windowEnd].t_ms; false: last point t_ms, or 0 when no points (?? fallback)

units.does: Chart start ms: first RR point, or the earlier of that and the earliest segment start on split nights.

branches.cond: fewer than 2 segment ranges or no min
branches.effect: return firstPoint.t_ms; else min(firstPoint.t_ms, earliest segment start)

units.does: Chart end ms: last RR point end, or the later of that and the latest segment end on split nights.

branches.cond: fewer than 2 segment ranges or no max
branches.effect: return lastPoint.endMs; else max(lastPoint.endMs, latest segment end)

Returns organized recovery zones for a session from the in-memory cache, or runs WindowSelector.findBestWindow for its side effect and caches selector.lastOrganizedZones.

branches.effect: true: return cached; false: run WindowSelector scan and cache result (including an empty array)

flags.text: Same cache-then-WindowSelector zone computation as RecoveryScoreDetailView.computeOrganizedZonesOnDemand (whose comment calls it 'Same fallback the legacy OvernightChartsView uses').

units.does: Fires a background detached task that persists computed zones into the archived session's analysisResult.

flags.text: docs/FLOWCHART.md says the on-demand organized-zone fallback re-runs the scan 'without rewriting the archive', but OvernightChartsView.loadOvernightStats calls backfillZonesToArchive, which re-archives the session with the computed zones (and posts flowRecoveryArchiveChanged).

units.does: Retrieves the archived session; if it has an analysisResult with nil organizedRecoveryZones, sets them (nil when empty) and re-archives the whole session. Errors are logged and swallowed.

branches.cond: session missing, analysisResult nil, or zones already set

branches.effect: writes nil (field stays empty, so every later launch rescans and re-attempts the backfill); else writes zones
catch: log a warning, nothing else; in-memory cache still serves this launch

flags.text: Read-modify-write via retrieve() then archive(_:) outside the archive lock, from a background task. SessionArchive.update documents that writing back a held copy undoes score/sleep updates made in between; a concurrent reanalysis or sleep refresh landing between the two calls is overwritten. archive(_:) also runs same-night merge (skipSameNightMerge: false) for a pure field backfill.

When the scan finds no zones, the guard still passes (field nil), the session is re-archived unchanged with nil zones and flowRecoveryArchiveChanged is broadcast; since nothing persists, every launch that opens the chart rescans and repeats this no-op archive write.

branches.effect: true: HK offsets (MillisecondOffset fallback 0 on unrepresentable interval); false: stored session values

rangeEnd set and point past it

units.does: Rolling RMSSD: for every 30th beat (last step snapped to final point) computes RMSSD over a 300-beat window centred on it via TimeDomainAnalyzer.peakScanRMSSD.

branches.effect: loop; empty series gives -1 so no iterations

branches.cond: not at last point and next step overshoots
branches.effect: snap i to last index; else i += 30

flags.text: docs/FLOWCHART.md says rolling RMSSD uses 5-min windows; code uses a 300-beat window (duration varies with HR).

units.does: Finds the max rolling RMSSD inside the 30–70% search band (falls back to all samples when none in band) and the mean of all rolling RMSSD.

branches.effect: use all samples for the max; else constrained set

flags.text: The PDF report reimplements the rolling 300-beat/30-step peak RMSSD scan (OvernightReportRenderer.calculatePeakRMSSD/scanForPeakRMSSD) with the 30-70% band taken over the recording only, while the screen takes it over the HealthKit sleep span when present; the PDF's peak RMSSD and its time can differ from the Overnight screen's Peak HRV card for the same night.

units.does: 30–70% slice of the HK sleep span (clamped to [0, recordingDurationMs]), or of 0..recordingDurationMs when HealthKit gave no boundaries.

branches.cond: HK sleep with start and end
branches.effect: boundaries from HK offsets; else 0..recordingDurationMs (stored session sleepStartMs/EndMs are ignored)

flags.text: Comment says the band matches WindowSelector's search region and uses the overall sleep envelope, but without HealthKit it ignores the stored session.sleepStartMs/sleepEndMs that the organized-zone scan and the 30%/70% markers use, so the peak marker and the dotted band lines can disagree (acknowledged at OvernightHRVChartCanvas.swift:481-485). It also clamps to recordingDurationMs measured from the first point, while offsets are from session.startDate.
